concepts.label: Homocystinuria is most often a cystathionine synthase defect, which raises both homocysteine and methionine; a methionine synthase defect raises homocysteine with normal methionine
concepts.arabicLabel: بيلة الهوموسيستين وارتفاع الهوموسيستين في الدم
concepts.definition: Homocystinuria is a group of autosomal recessive diseases involving defects in the metabolism of homocysteine. The commonest cause is a defect in cystathionine synthase, the pyridoxal phosphate-dependent enzyme that converts homocysteine to cystathionine; a defect of the enzyme or of vitamin B6 gives high plasma homocysteine and high plasma methionine, low plasma cysteine — which becomes an essential amino acid in these patients — and excretion of large amounts of homocystine, two homocysteine molecules joined by a disulfide linkage. The other cause is a defect in methionine synthase, which converts homocysteine to methionine using vitamin B12 and tetrahydrofolate; a defect of the enzyme, of folate or of B12 gives high homocysteine with normal methionine, and the same homocystinuria. Raised homocysteine modifies LDL and collagen, producing endothelial injury, atherogenesis, coronary artery disease, thromboembolic disorders and hypertension, together with osteoporosis, mental retardation, and dislocation or complete detachment of the lens. Treatment is restriction of methionine intake and a diet rich in cysteine with vitamins B6, B12 and folate.
concepts.explicitObjective: Name cystathionine synthase as the commonest deficient enzyme in raised plasma homocysteine, and use the plasma methionine level to separate a cystathionine synthase defect from a methionine synthase defect.
concepts.pitfalls: Confusing homocystinuria with cystinuria. The names are close and the mechanisms are opposite: homocystinuria is a metabolic defect with an abnormal plasma, cystinuria is a transport defect with a normal plasma. Forgetting that methionine rises only in the cystathionine synthase form — that single value is what the examiner uses to separate the two causes. Choosing glutathione reductase because glutathione contains cysteine, which is downstream of homocysteine; reducing glutathione consumes no homocysteine. Expecting renal stones: the damage here is vascular, skeletal, ocular and neurological.
moduleSubjectPaths: 103 BMS > Biochemistry > Individual amino acid Metabolism > Methionine
originalWording: "The most common cause is a defect in the enzyme cystathionine synthase, which converts homocysteine to cystathionine, and requires PLP as coenzyme. In this condition (defect of the enzyme or vitamin B6), the disease is characterized by: High plasma levels of homocysteine and methionine. Low plasma levels of cysteine which is considered essential amino acid."
uncertainty: The book presents homocystinuria as a group of autosomal recessive diseases but gives no incidence, no age of presentation and no genetic detail beyond the inheritance pattern. It also does not distinguish the severe inherited disease from the mild raised homocysteine of dietary B12 or folate deficiency, and treats the same two enzyme defects as the explanation for both, which is a simplification a reviewer may want to flag for later years.
evidenceGaps: Supported by the department book alone, printed page 99 and the Summary of Amino Acid Metabolism on printed page 107. No independent verification against an international biochemistry reference has been attached. The book gives no target plasma homocysteine, no dose for the vitamin supplementation it recommends, and no evidence that lowering homocysteine changes the vascular outcome — the causal claim about atherogenesis is stated, not evidenced, on the page.

concepts.label: Absorbed amino acids join one common pool with an anabolic and a catabolic fate, and only the anabolic fate keeps the nitrogen
concepts.arabicLabel: مصير الأحماض الأمينية الممتصة ومخزون الأحماض الأمينية
concepts.definition: Absorbed amino acids mix with those released from body protein and those synthesised in the body to form one common amino acid pool, drawn on for both anabolism and catabolism. The anabolic fate is synthesis of proteins and of other nitrogenous substances — glutathione, adrenaline, thyroxine, melanin, niacin, purines, pyrimidines, amino sugars and the nitrogenous bases of phospholipids. The catabolic fate begins by cleaving the amino acid into ammonia, mostly converted to urea, and a carbon skeleton that may become glucose, ketone bodies, or CO2 and water.
concepts.explicitObjective: Sort a named fate of the amino acid pool into the anabolic or the catabolic branch, and give the rule that decides it — whether the nitrogen is kept in a useful molecule or routed to excretion.
concepts.pitfalls: Counting urea synthesis or glucose synthesis as anabolic because a molecule is being made. Both are catabolic: urea is how the nitrogen leaves, and gluconeogenesis acts on a carbon skeleton whose nitrogen has already been stripped off.

concepts.label: Tyrosine is the precursor of the catecholamines, melanin and the thyroid hormones, and DOPA is where the first two part company
concepts.arabicLabel: مشتقات التيروسين: الكاتيكولامينات والميلانين وهرمونات الغدة الدرقية
concepts.definition: Tyrosine is hydroxylated to dihydroxyphenylalanine (DOPA) by tyrosine hydroxylase, which needs the same factors as phenylalanine hydroxylase, and DOPA is the precursor of the catecholamines — dopamine, noradrenaline and adrenaline. DOPA produced in melanocytes is used instead for the synthesis of melanin by tyrosinase, so the same intermediate serves the transmitter pathway in one tissue and the pigment pathway in another. The third derivative bypasses DOPA altogether: tyrosine residues of thyroglobulin are iodinated to monoiodotyrosine and diiodotyrosine, and two diiodotyrosine couple to give T4 while one of each gives T3.
concepts.explicitObjective: Name tyrosine as the precursor of the catecholamines, melanin and the thyroid hormones; place DOPA as the branch point between the catecholamine and melanin routes; and name the enzyme that makes DOPA and the one that consumes it.
concepts.pitfalls: Assigning serotonin or melatonin to tyrosine. Both come from tryptophan, and melanin and melatonin are two letters apart — the most reliable confusion in the chapter. GABA is not on the list either; that is decarboxylated from glutamate. The other error is routing the thyroid hormones through DOPA: they are built on tyrosine residues still bound in thyroglobulin, and no hydroxylase is involved.

concepts.label: Carcinoid tumour overproduces serotonin, so blood and urine 5-HIAA rise — and pellagra may develop because tryptophan is diverted away from nicotinic acid
concepts.arabicLabel: الورم السرطاوي وارتفاع حمض الهيدروكسي إندول أسيتيك
concepts.definition: A carcinoid tumour, or argentaffinoma, is a tumour of the argentaffin cells of the gastrointestinal tract, and it overproduces serotonin. Both serotonin and its metabolite 5-hydroxyindole-acetic acid, 5-HIAA, are present at increased levels in blood and urine; 5-HIAA is formed from serotonin by monoamine oxidase. The tumour has a second consequence on the other branch of the same amino acid: pellagra may develop, because tryptophan metabolism is shunted towards the synthesis of serotonin and its metabolites by the tumour cells, with a marked decrease in nicotinic acid synthesis.
concepts.explicitObjective: Name 5-HIAA as the metabolite raised in carcinoid tumour and the enzyme that makes it, and explain on a biochemical basis why the same patient may develop pellagra.
concepts.pitfalls: Choosing melatonin because it is genuinely downstream of serotonin. Melatonin is made in the pineal body, and the argentaffin cells of the gut have no melatonin-forming machinery. The other trap is nicotinic acid, which moves in the opposite direction to 5-HIAA in this patient: a student who knows the tumour involves tryptophan but has not tracked which branch gains and which loses picks the branch that is being starved.

originalWording: "Carcinoid tumor or argentaffinoma (tumor of argentaffin cells in the gastrointestinal tract) presents with increased levels of serotonin and its metabolite, 5-hydroxyindole-acetic acid (5-HIAA) in both blood and urine. 5-HIAA is formed from serotonin by monoamine Oxidase (MAO) enzyme."

"Pellagra may develop in carcinoid tumor because tryptophan metabolism is shunted toward the synthesis of serotonin and its metabolites by the tumor cells, with marked decrease in nicotinic acid synthesis."
uncertainty: The book says both serotonin and 5-HIAA are raised in blood and urine, and does not say which is measured in practice or why. That urinary 5-HIAA is the usual test because it is a stable end product is a clinical convention the book does not print, and it is not asserted on this record.
evidenceGaps: Evidence must be attached before publication.
Supported by the department book and the department question book only
no independent clinical or biochemistry reference has been attached.

The book describes carcinoid tumour biochemically and gives it no clinical syndrome at all — no flushing, no diarrhoea, no wheezing, no site predilection, no treatment and no prognosis. None of that is claimed here, although the question's vignette supplies it as authored clinical context.
It does not say how much tryptophan a tumour must divert before pellagra appears, nor whether dietary niacin protects against it.

concepts.label: The three jaundices are told apart by which bilirubin rises and which enzyme rises with it
concepts.arabicLabel: تصنيف اليرقان حسب نوع البيليروبين وتغيرات الإنزيمات
concepts.definition: Jaundice is classified by which form of bilirubin predominates in serum. In haemolytic jaundice bilirubin production outruns the liver's capacity to excrete it, so unconjugated (indirect) bilirubin rises while the conjugated fraction stays normal; the book records no enzyme change for it. In obstructive jaundice conjugated (direct) bilirubin regurgitates into blood and alkaline phosphatase is raised. In hepatocellular jaundice both fractions rise — the damaged liver conjugates less, and swollen cells block the canaliculi — and ALT and AST are raised because liver cells are being destroyed.
concepts.explicitObjective: Complete a three-by-three table of haemolytic, obstructive and hepatocellular jaundice against the bilirubin fraction elevated and the serum enzyme change in each.
concepts.pitfalls: Filling the enzyme column for haemolytic jaundice with something. The book gives no enzyme change there, because nothing is obstructed and no hepatocyte is damaged — the abnormality is upstream of the liver. Writing "ALP" in every row that involves the biliary tree is the other error; ALP marks obstruction, and ALT and AST mark hepatocyte damage.

concepts.label: In obstructive jaundice the stool is clay coloured because no stercobilin reaches it, and the urine is dark because conjugated bilirubin does
concepts.definition: Obstruction of the biliary passages — by gallstones, by cancer of the head of the pancreas, or by inflammation of the pancreas or of the passages themselves — stops conjugated bilirubin reaching the intestine and forces it back into the blood. Two consequences follow directly. Stercobilin, which is what makes stool brown, disappears from the faeces, so the stool is clay coloured. Conjugated bilirubin is water-soluble and not bound to albumin, so the kidney excretes it and the urine becomes dark brown. The urine also contains bile salts, and serum alkaline phosphatase is raised.
concepts.explicitObjective: Explain, from what happens to bilirubin, why the stool is pale and the urine is dark in obstructive jaundice, naming the pigment missing from each.
concepts.pitfalls: Saying the urine is dark because of unconjugated bilirubin. Unconjugated bilirubin is bound to albumin and cannot be filtered — that is why haemolytic jaundice is called acholuric. Only conjugated bilirubin appears in urine, and it is the one that rises when the duct is blocked.

concepts.label: Glycolysis is the only source of ATP in the red cell, because the red cell has no mitochondria
aliases: Substrate level phosphorylation in red cells
Why red cells depend on glycolysis
Methaemoglobin and the glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase step
concepts.arabicLabel: أهمية تحلل الجلوكوز لكرات الدم الحمراء
arabicAliases: مصدر الطاقة الوحيد في كرة الدم الحمراء

concepts.definition: Red cells have no mitochondria, so they cannot use the electron transport chain and glycolysis is their only source of ATP, produced by substrate-level phosphorylation. Glycolysis does a second job for them as well: the NADH+H⁺ made at the glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase step keeps the iron of haemoglobin in the ferrous state, because ferric haem makes methaemoglobin, which cannot carry oxygen.
concepts.explicitObjective: State the two reasons the book gives for why glycolysis matters to a red cell, and explain why a red cell cannot fall back on any other pathway for ATP.
concepts.pitfalls: Answering only "for energy". The book gives two points and the mark scheme follows it: ATP by substrate-level phosphorylation, and NADH to keep haemoglobin iron ferrous. Leaving out the methaemoglobin half is the usual way to lose half of this mark.

concepts.label: Crigler-Najjar type I is a complete loss of glucuronyl transferase, and that completeness is why phenobarbital cannot help
concepts.definition: Crigler-Najjar type I is an autosomal recessive, complete or near-complete absence of UDP-glucuronyl transferase, so almost no bilirubin can be conjugated; serum unconjugated bilirubin climbs past the albumin carrying capacity of about 20 mg/dL and kernicterus is the expected outcome. Type II is a partial deficiency with residual enzyme activity, and the bilirubin generally stays below that threshold. The discriminator worth holding is the response to phenobarbital: the drug works by inducing glucuronyl transferase, and induction can only increase the amount of an enzyme the cell is still able to make, so patients with type I do not respond while patients with type II do.
concepts.explicitObjective: Distinguish Crigler-Najjar type I from type II by completeness of enzyme deficiency, serum bilirubin level, inheritance and response to phenobarbital, and explain from the mechanism of induction why an inducer cannot rescue a complete deficiency.
concepts.pitfalls: Learning the two types as an arbitrary pair of descriptions and then guessing at the phenobarbital row. The reasoning runs the other way: decide first whether any enzyme remains, and the drug response, the bilirubin level and the kernicterus risk all follow. The second error is calling type I autosomal dominant — a complete loss of activity needs two defective alleles, since one working allele would leave residual enzyme, which is type II.

concepts.label: Faecal stercobilinogen measures how much bilirubin reached the gut, so it rises in haemolysis, falls in hepatocellular jaundice and disappears in obstruction
concepts.arabicLabel: الستيركوبيلينوجين البرازي كمؤشر على كمية البيليروبين الواصلة للأمعاء
concepts.definition: In the large intestine, bacterial enzymes release bilirubin from glucuronic acid and reduce it successively to colourless stercobilinogen. Most of it is excreted in stool and oxidised by the oxygen of the air to brown stercobilin, which is what gives stool its colour; about 10 per cent is reabsorbed and returned to the liver in portal blood to be re-excreted in bile, the enterohepatic circulation; and a very little escapes to the systemic circulation and reaches the kidney as colourless urobilinogen, oxidised in air to the yellow urobilin that gives urine its normal colour. Because all of it comes from bilirubin delivered in bile, the amount in stool tracks the delivery: in haemolytic jaundice more bilirubin is made and secreted, so stercobilin increases and the stool becomes dark brown; in hepatocellular jaundice less is secreted, so it usually decreases and the stool is faint; and in obstruction none arrives at all, so stercobilin disappears and the stool is clay coloured.
concepts.explicitObjective: Predict faecal stercobilinogen from the amount of conjugated bilirubin reaching the intestine, and give the stool and urine picture of haemolytic jaundice — dark stool, urobilinogen-positive but bilirubin-negative urine.
concepts.pitfalls: Reasoning from the serum bilirubin instead of from what reaches the gut. Haemolytic jaundice raises serum bilirubin and *raises* stercobilinogen; obstructive jaundice also raises serum bilirubin and abolishes it. The two go opposite ways because what matters downstream is delivery in bile, not concentration in blood. The second error is expecting bilirubin in the urine of a haemolytic patient — the excess there is unconjugated and albumin-bound, so it cannot be filtered, which is why the book calls that jaundice acholuric even while urinary urobilinogen rises.

concepts.label: Lead blocks haem synthesis at both ends of the pathway — ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase — which is why the anaemia is microcytic and iron does not fix it
concepts.arabicLabel: تأثير التسمم بالرصاص على تخليق الهيم
arabicAliases: تثبيط إنزيم نازعة هيدرات حمض دلتا أمينوليفولينيك
concepts.definition: The department book records lead's effect on haem metabolism as a note in its own right: in lead poisoning, lead inhibits ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase. The two enzymes sit at opposite ends of the pathway. ALA dehydratase is step 2, condensing two molecules of ALA into porphobilinogen in the cytosol, so blocking it backs ALA up. Ferrochelatase is step 8, inserting ferrous iron into the centre of the protoporphyrin ring in the mitochondrion, so blocking it leaves protoporphyrin unable to become haem and leaves the iron unused.
concepts.explicitObjective: Name the two enzymes of haem synthesis that lead inhibits, place each at its step in the pathway, and explain why the resulting anaemia is microcytic and does not respond to iron.
concepts.pitfalls: Expecting a lead-poisoned patient to improve on iron. Iron supply was never the problem — the enzyme that inserts it is poisoned, so the iron accumulates unused. The other error is reaching for megaloblastic: interference with haem synthesis leaves the cell dividing normally but unable to fill itself with haemoglobin, which is a microcytic picture, while megaloblastic anaemia is a failure of DNA synthesis from folate or B12 deficiency.
moduleSubjectPaths: 103 BMS > Biochemistry > Heme Metabolism > Biosynthesis of Heme
originalWording: "N.B. In lead poisoning, lead inhibits ALA dehydratase and ferrochelatase enzymes."
"Insertion of the ferrous iron into the center of the protoporphyrin ring is catalyzed by ferrochelatase (heme synthase) to form heme. Ferrochelatase is inhibited by lead."
uncertainty: The book names the two inhibited enzymes and nothing else about lead poisoning — no blood lead threshold, no red cell morphology, no treatment, and no statement that the anaemia is microcytic. The microcytic morphology is standard haematology and is the reasoning the question's key requires, but it is not this book's own word and is flagged as such.
evidenceGaps: Supported by the department book only for the enzyme inhibition itself. The consequence taught alongside it in the question book — a microcytic anaemia unresponsive to iron — is not stated in this textbook, and no source in the evidence store has been attached for it. No evidence claim is authored for this concept in this batch.

concepts.label: Conjugated bilirubin is water-soluble, and every other row of the book's comparison table follows from that one property
concepts.arabicLabel: البيليروبين المقترن: قابل للذوبان في الماء ومباشر التفاعل
concepts.definition: Conjugated bilirubin is the form the liver has attached glucuronic acid to, and the book calls it cholebilirubin because bile is its route of excretion. It is mostly polar and water-soluble, and because it is soluble it is not bound to plasma proteins; being unbound and soluble it is excreted by the kidney and appears in urine; and being polar it does not pass the blood-brain barrier, so it does not cause brain damage. In the Van den Bergh reaction it reacts directly with the reagent, within one minute, which is why it is called direct-reacting, and its normal serum level is below 0.3 mg/dL. Unconjugated bilirubin is the mirror image on every one of those rows, and in haemolytic jaundice it is the unconjugated fraction that rises while the conjugated fraction stays normal.
concepts.explicitObjective: Given any statement about a form of bilirubin — protein binding, renal excretion, blood-brain barrier crossing, Van den Bergh behaviour, or which jaundice raises it — decide which form it describes, by asking first whether that form is soluble.
concepts.pitfalls: Believing that conjugated bilirubin causes kernicterus. Only unconjugated bilirubin crosses the blood-brain barrier, because it is hydrophobic, and it does so when its plasma level exceeds the carrying capacity of albumin at about 20 mg/dL. A student who reverses this will misjudge which jaundiced neonate is at risk. The second reversal is expecting conjugated bilirubin to rise in haemolysis — the book's own table records it as normal there.
moduleSubjectPaths: 103 BMS > Biochemistry > Heme Metabolism > Blood Bilirubin
originalWording: "Being water-soluble, conjugated bilirubin is not bound to plasma proteins
thus, it can be excreted in urine but does not pass the blood brain barrier."
"The water-soluble conjugated bilirubin (as it is not bound to proteins) reacts rapidly with the reagent (within one minute) and is said to be 'direct reacting.'"
uncertainty: The book's table gives "mostly nonpolar" and "mostly polar" rather than absolute statements, and it does not say what the residual polarity of unconjugated bilirubin is or how much of it is unbound in plasma. It also gives no reference range for conjugated bilirubin other than "<0.3 mg/dL", with no lower bound.

No independent verification against an international clinical chemistry reference has been attached, and no evidence claim is authored for this concept in this batch. The book's summary table on printed page 123 leaves the enzyme row for haemolytic jaundice blank rather than writing "normal"

concepts.label: Adenosine deaminase deficiency raises dATP, which shuts down ribonucleotide reductase and leaves lymphocytes unable to divide — severe combined immunodeficiency
concepts.arabicLabel: عوز نازعة أمين الأدينوزين والعوز المناعي المشترك الشديد
concepts.definition: Adenosine deaminase converts adenosine to inosine at the start of purine catabolism. When it is deficient the substrate accumulates and is phosphorylated onward, and the resulting high levels of dATP inhibit ribonucleotide reductase — the enzyme complex that makes deoxyribonucleotides and is active only during DNA synthesis. DNA synthesis then fails, so white blood cells cannot proliferate, T-cell and B-cell function is impaired, and the condition is associated with severe combined immunodeficiency. Plasma urate falls at the same time, because catabolism is blocked before uric acid can be formed: this is a purine defect whose damage is immunological rather than articular.
concepts.explicitObjective: Trace the chain from adenosine deaminase deficiency through dATP and ribonucleotide reductase to failed lymphocyte proliferation, and say why plasma urate falls rather than rises.
concepts.pitfalls: Assuming a defect in the purine pathway must present as gout, and answering HGPRT. HGPRT deficiency is the other severe purine enzyme defect in this chapter, but its extra-articular damage is neurological and its urate goes up; adenosine deaminase deficiency damages the immune system and its urate goes down. The second error is calling ribonucleotide reductase a purine enzyme — it reduces both purine and pyrimidine ribonucleotides, which is why losing it stops DNA synthesis outright rather than starving the cell of one base.
moduleSubjectPaths: 103 BMS > Biochemistry > Metabolism of purines and pyrimidines > Disorders of Purine Metabolism
originalWording: "It is caused mainly by adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency. The high levels of dATP inhibit ribonucleotide reductase, which inhibits DNA synthesis. Therefore, white blood cells cannot proliferate resulting in impairment of T-cell and B-cell functions. It is associated with severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID)."
"This is catalyzed by an enzyme complex termed ribonucleotide reductase which is active only during DNA synthesis and inhibited mainly by dATP."
uncertainty: The book says dATP accumulates but does not spell out the intermediate step — that it is deoxyadenosine, spared by the missing deaminase and phosphorylated by adenosine kinase, that becomes dATP. It also gives no age of onset, no inheritance pattern and no treatment for the condition, and does not say whether the immunodeficiency or the hypouricaemia presents first.
evidenceGaps: The whole mechanism is stated outright by the department book, and it is the one record in this batch that needs no inference. What the book does not carry is purine nucleoside phosphorylase deficiency, which the question book's key names alongside adenosine deaminase as a second cause of immune dysfunction

that half rests on the question book and on standard references and is deliberately not asserted here as this book's teaching. No independent verification against an immunology reference has been attached.

concepts.label: Cystinuria is a genetic defect in the dibasic amino acid transporter, so cystine, arginine, ornithine and lysine are not reabsorbed and cystine forms stones
aliases: Most common genetic error of amino acid transport
concepts.arabicLabel: البيلة السيستينية وخلل نقل الأحماض الأمينية ثنائية القاعدة
arabicAliases: خلل ناقل الأحماض الأمينية ثنائية القاعدة
concepts.definition: Cystinuria is the most common genetic error of amino acid transport. A genetic defect in the transporter of the dibasic amino acids causes failure to transport cystine, arginine, ornithine and lysine across the renal proximal tubules, so all four are excreted in the urine. Cystine is the least soluble of the four; it precipitates in the renal tubules, crystallises as the characteristic hexagonal crystals seen in urine, and forms cystine stones. Treatment follows directly from the mechanism — alkalinisation of the urine and ingestion of plenty of fluids make cystine more soluble so that it is washed out of the urinary tract rather than deposited in it.
concepts.explicitObjective: Identify cystinuria as a defect of dibasic amino acid transport rather than of synthesis or degradation, name the four amino acids that appear in the urine, and justify alkalinisation and fluids from the mechanism.
concepts.pitfalls: Answering that the defect is in synthesis, when plasma amino acids are normal and only the urine is abnormal — that pattern is the signature of a transport problem. Answering acidic amino acid transport: glutamate and aspartate do not appear. Including methionine among the four: it is a neutral sulfur amino acid handled by a different transporter, and it is tempting only because it is upstream of cysteine in a pathway the transporter knows nothing about. Answering that disulfide bond formation fails — cystine is two cysteines joined by a disulfide, but making that bond is normal here. Confusing cystinuria with homocystinuria, whose plasma is abnormal and whose damage is vascular and ocular rather than renal.
moduleSubjectPaths: 103 BMS > Biochemistry > Individual amino acid Metabolism > Cysteine
originalWording: "Cystinuria: It is the most common genetic error of amino acid transport. Cause and manifestations: a genetic defect in the transporter of dibasic amino acids leading to failure of transport of these amino acids (cystine, arginine, ornithine, and lysine) across the renal proximal tubules and are excreted in urine."
uncertainty: The book names the transporter only as "the transporter of dibasic amino acids" and gives no gene, no protein name and no inheritance pattern. It also does not say whether the same transporter is affected in the intestine, which is standard teaching elsewhere and is not asserted here. Whether the plasma cystine is normal is implied by calling the defect one of transport but is not stated on the page.
evidenceGaps: Supported by the department book alone, printed page 97, "Metabolic Disorder of Cysteine Metabolism — Cystinuria". No independent verification against an international reference has been attached. The book gives no incidence figure for a disorder it calls the most common of its class, and offers no second-line treatment beyond alkalinisation and fluids.

concepts.label: Uraemia is failure to excrete urea, not failure to make it: renal failure raises plasma urea, while hepatic failure lowers it and raises ammonia
concepts.arabicLabel: اليوريميا: فشل في الإخراج لا في التصنيع
concepts.definition: Urea is synthesised only in the liver and travels in the blood, at a normal plasma level of 10 to 50 mg/dL, to the kidneys, where it passes into the urine. Production and excretion are therefore the jobs of two different organs, and they fail in opposite directions. In renal failure the liver goes on making urea normally but the product cannot leave, so plasma urea rises: that is uraemia, and it is why blood urea is a marker of renal and not of hepatic function. In hepatic failure the cycle itself fails, so ammonia remains in the blood as hyperammonaemia, or ammonia intoxication, while the plasma urea level falls; normal blood ammonia is below 0.05 mg/dL. Acquired hyperammonaemia occurs in liver cirrhosis, which may follow hepatitis, biliary obstruction or alcoholism, and the hereditary forms are rare deficiencies of the urea cycle enzymes, most severe when one of the first two reactions is affected.
concepts.explicitObjective: Predict what happens to plasma urea and to plasma ammonia in renal failure and in hepatic failure, and say which of the two failures is uraemia.
concepts.pitfalls: Reasoning that liver disease is serious, so urea must be high. Cirrhosis damages the organ that makes urea, so plasma urea falls and what rises is ammonia. The second trap is diabetes mellitus: it raises protein catabolism and so raises urea production, but healthy kidneys excrete the surplus, and uraemia follows only once diabetic nephropathy has damaged the kidney — at which point the cause is the renal failure.
moduleSubjectPaths: 103 BMS > Biochemistry > General protein Metabolism > Metabolism of Ammonia
originalWording: "The urea formed by the liver goes, via the blood (plasma level 10-50 mg/dL), to the kidneys to be excreted in the urine."
"In renal failure, the plasma level of urea increases. In hepatic failure, ammonia remains in the blood, leading to hyperammonemia (ammonia intoxication) with decrease of plasma urea level."
uncertainty: The book gives one plasma urea range, 10 to 50 mg/dL, without naming an assay, a population or a unit conversion, and gives no threshold above which the word uraemia applies. It also does not say whether "renal failure" here means acute, chronic or either. Nothing beyond the direction of change is asserted.
evidenceGaps: Evidence must be attached before publication
no claim or citation is authored by this batch.

Supported by the department book and the department question book only. No independent clinical chemistry reference range has been attached, and the department range is not converted to SI units anywhere.
The book never states that blood urea is used clinically as a test of renal function

concepts.label: Hypouricaemia is a block in purine catabolism, and the department's textbook and its question book name different enzymes for it
aliases: Adenosine deaminase deficiency and low urate
concepts.definition: Hypouricaemia is a plasma urate below the fasting reference range, and every cause in this chapter is a block in the catabolic route before uric acid is formed. The department textbook gives one cause: adenosine deaminase deficiency, which stops adenosine becoming inosine, raises dATP and produces severe combined immunodeficiency. The department question book's printed key gives another: xanthine oxidase deficiency, which removes the two final oxidations — hypoxanthine to xanthine and xanthine to uric acid — so uric acid cannot be formed and the more soluble precursors are excreted instead. Both are genuine, and the direction is what matters: a block upstream of uric acid lowers urate, while every cause of gout raises it.
concepts.explicitObjective: Name the catabolic enzyme blocks that lower plasma urate, explain in each case why urate falls, and separate them from the causes of gout by the direction urate moves.
concepts.pitfalls: Reading a purine enzyme deficiency as automatically a cause of gout. Complete HGPRT deficiency raises urate and adenosine deaminase deficiency lowers it, and both are deficiencies in the same chapter. The other error is expecting the textbook's answer on a question paper: a student who has learned the book's sentence looks for adenosine deaminase among the options and does not find it, because the question book keys this to xanthine oxidase instead.
moduleSubjectPaths: 103 BMS > Biochemistry > Metabolism of purines and pyrimidines > Disorders of Purine Metabolism
originalWording: "II- Hypouricemia — It is caused mainly by adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency."
"The high levels of dATP inhibit ribonucleotide reductase, which inhibits DNA synthesis."
conflicts: The department textbook states that hypouricaemia "is caused mainly by adenosine deaminase (ADA) deficiency" and names no other cause.
The department question book's printed key for the same question gives xanthine oxidase deficiency, and adenosine deaminase deficiency is not among the four options it offers.
uncertainty: Whether the two departmental sources actually disagree, or whether the question book is simply testing a second cause the textbook omits, cannot be settled from either document. Both enzyme blocks genuinely lower plasma urate, so both keys are defensible

what is unclear is which the faculty expects when the two appear in the same option list, and neither source says how far below the reference range a plasma urate must fall to be called hypouricaemic.
evidenceGaps: The adenosine deaminase half is stated outright by the department book. The xanthine oxidase half is not in the book at all — the book never names a xanthine oxidase deficiency as an entity — and rests on the question book's printed key together with the book's own catabolic diagram, in which xanthine oxidase performs the last two oxidations. support_mode is recorded as inferred for that reason, and the record must not be published until a faculty reviewer decides which cause the department teaches.

concepts.label: Every cause of gout either makes more urate or excretes less of it, so a block at xanthine oxidase — which makes less — cannot be one
concepts.arabicLabel: أسباب النقرس: زيادة الإنتاج أو نقص الإخراج
concepts.definition: The book splits hyperuricaemia, and with it gout, into exactly two mechanisms. Overproduction covers a diet rich in nucleoprotein such as meat, liver and kidney; primary metabolic gout from genetic disorders — defects of PRPP synthetase that leave the enzyme superactive or resistant to feedback inhibition, partial deficiency of HGPRT, Lesch-Nyhan syndrome from complete HGPRT deficiency, and Von Gierke's disease, in which glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency enhances purine synthesis and degradation while decreasing uric acid excretion; and secondary metabolic gout from diseases that raise purine catabolism, such as cancer, leukaemia and psoriasis. Decreased excretion — renal gout — covers primary or congenital renal disease, acquired renal disease, and alcohol. Because uric acid is made by xanthine oxidase, a deficiency of that enzyme moves urate in the opposite direction and cannot be a cause of gout; it is the exception that shows the classification is about the direction urate moves.
concepts.explicitObjective: Sort a named disorder into overproduction or decreased excretion of urate, and explain why xanthine oxidase deficiency belongs to neither.
concepts.pitfalls: Treating "a purine enzyme defect" as automatically a cause of gout. The classification is not about which enzyme is affected but about which way urate moves, and three of the enzyme defects in this chapter — xanthine oxidase, adenosine deaminase and purine nucleoside phosphorylase — lower it. The second error is filing Von Gierke's disease under decreased excretion because the book's sentence ends with excretion; the book lists it under increased production, and it does both.
moduleSubjectPaths: 103 BMS > Biochemistry > Metabolism of purines and pyrimidines > Disorders of Purine Metabolism
originalWording: "Hyperuricemia or elevated serum urate levels results from over production (metabolic) or decreased excretion (renal)."

"a- Defects of PRPP synthetase: Due to genetic mutation, the enzyme is either superactive or resistant to feedback inhibition. b- Partial deficiency of HGPRTase of purine salvage system. c- Lesch-Nyhan Syndrome: Complete deficiency of HGPRTase. d- Von Gierke's disease (Glucose 6-phosphatase deficiency) due to enhanced synthesis and degradation of purine and decreased excretion of uric acid"
"1) Primary Renal Gout: It is due to primary or congenital renal disease. 2) Secondary Renal Gout: It is due to acquired renal disease."
uncertainty: The book gives no relative frequency for the causes it lists, so a student cannot tell from it whether primary metabolic gout is common or rare beside dietary and renal causes. It also does not say how much residual HGPRT activity separates "partial deficiency" from Lesch-Nyhan.
evidenceGaps: The classification and every listed cause are the book's own. The exception — that xanthine oxidase deficiency cannot cause gout — is not in the book, which never names the deficiency as an entity

it is inferred from the book's own catabolic diagram, in which xanthine oxidase makes uric acid, and from its account of allopurinol as a deliberate partial version of the same block. The inference rests additionally on the question book's printed key, which is curriculum signal rather than evidence, and support_mode is recorded as inferred for that reason.

qualifiers.why: The cited growth claim separates growth from development in one sentence, and the milestones claim defines the markers of the second. One measures size, the other capability.
Monitoring is how growth is observed, and both cited claims are about the same quantity — one defines it, one records it.
Intake determines whether growth proceeds. The cited feeding claim states that requirement outgrows milk at six months and does not name growth as the outcome.
The cited delay definition is stated in terms of failing to attain milestones, so the markers must be understood first.
Developmental screening is how delay is found in an asymptomatic child. Both endpoints are cited; neither source connects them.
One cited claim defines a screening test, the other defines a screening programme of which the test is a single component.

Screening is the secondary level of prevention. The cited claims define screening and the primary level; the source's secondary-prevention sentence is cardiovascular-specific and was not used, so the link is unevidenced.
Ordered as teaching sequence only. Both cited claims are present and the article argues these run on different timetables rather than one causing the other, which is why this edge stays unverified.
The cited staging claim describes tracking secondary sex characteristics during puberty, which the other claim defines.

Separation and identity formation involve experiment, which is where risk behaviour arises. The cited adolescent claim calls separation normal and says nothing about risk; the other names an intervention. Kept unverified and at low confidence because the causal step is the article's reasoning.

A brief intervention targets a modifiable risk factor in someone still healthy, which is the cited definition of primary prevention. The connection is inference from the two definitions rather than a stated link.

Immunisation prevents infections that can cause developmental delay. Both endpoints are cited, the chain has an uncited step in the middle, and it is kept at low confidence rather than dropped because students meet the link.
The cited growth claim pairs growth charts with developmental screening as the means of early identification, and the screening claim defines what such a test is.
A newborn programme acts before disease declares itself. Both endpoints are cited; the level it belongs to is secondary prevention, which has no usable definition in this batch.
The cited stunting definition names inappropriate infant and young child feeding among its causes, and the feeding claim is the recommendation that names.
The cited ICF claim states that disability is the umbrella term for restrictions in exactly the components the functioning claim defines.
Daily activities are the executed tasks the ICF calls activity, and both cited claims describe the same level.
The ICF pairs the two terms deliberately and students use them interchangeably. Both cited definitions are present and they are complements, not synonyms.
WHO's cited framing places disability partly in environmental factors, and the cited accommodation definition is the modification of those factors so rights can be exercised equally.
Communication is the commonest access need an adjustment addresses. Both endpoints are cited and neither source connects them; the ordering is editorial.
The cited accommodation definition is written for persons with disabilities, so the term must be understood before the duty is.
Lost daily activities are what an informal caregiver performs instead. Both endpoints are cited; neither source states the link.

Available care is one of the personal and environmental factors WHO's cited definition names. Reading a caregiver as one of those factors is inference from the definition rather than a stated instance.
Preventing occupational disease prevents the impairments that disable. Both endpoints are cited and the chain between them is not stated by either source.
The cited occupational claim describes services whose task is prevention, and the cited primary-prevention claim defines acting on risk factors before disease begins.
Function describes what a person does now; frailty describes what happens when something is demanded of them. Both endpoints are cited and the contrast is the library's, not a source's.
Physical performance is one of the three traits the cited sarcopenia diagnosis names, and daily activities are how performance shows itself. The connection is inference across two sources.
Not understanding health information is a participation restriction. Both endpoints are cited and neither source classifies health literacy within the ICF.
The factors have to be known before they can be combined into an estimate, and both cited claims are about the same set.
The cited WHO principle states that decisions about preventive action should be guided by risk estimation, which is what the prevention claim defines.

Behavioural factors accelerate the accumulation of damage that the cited ageing claim describes. Both endpoints are cited, the link is not stated by either source, and it is kept at low confidence rather than dropped because students meet it.
Heritable illness in relatives is one of the inputs to an estimate of total risk. Both endpoints are cited; neither source names the family history as an input.

The cited family-history definition includes current family health and relationship data, and the cited caregiver definition describes a family member providing care — the same people, recorded for two purposes.
A school setting acts on healthy children before disease begins, which is the cited definition of primary prevention. Both endpoints are cited and neither source classifies school health as a level.
School is where most adolescent development happens and where peers become the reference group. Both endpoints are cited; the connection is the library's.
Counting risk factors is mistaken for estimating risk. Both cited claims are present and the second is explicitly about estimation rather than enumeration.
The bilayer is what makes a membrane selectively permeable, so the structure must be understood before the property.
Selective permeability is a property of the membrane, not a separate structure.
A receptor is a membrane protein; the membrane must be understood first.
Chromosomes are held in the nucleus, so chromosomal disorders are disorders of nuclear content. The cited claim establishes the nucleus holds DNA but does not itself assert the link.
The inheritance pattern follows from the organelle carrying its own genome and coming only from the egg.
The mitotic spindle is built from microtubules, so the cytoskeleton participates in the cycle. The cited claim defines the cycle but does not assert the spindle link.
Second messengers are generated in response to receptor activation, so the receptor step precedes them.
The messenger is part of the signalling cascade the receptor initiates.
Pharmacodynamics is largely the study of drug action at receptors.
Both are cell death; one is programmed and controlled, the other accidental and uncontrolled. Both definitions are independently cited.
The most examined confusion in general pathology, and the reverse direction of the contrast above.
The intrinsic pathway begins with cytochrome c release from the mitochondrion. The cited claim covers the caspase machinery, not the mitochondrial trigger.
A cell failing a checkpoint and unable to repair is directed to apoptosis. The cited claim defines the cycle but not the checkpoint outcome.
Reversible injury precedes necrosis on the injury continuum. The cited claim defines necrosis but does not assert the sequence.
Adaptation succeeds in maintaining homeostasis; injury is what follows when it does not.
Both definitions are independently cited and differ on duration, cell population and outcome.
Inflammation clears the wound before the proliferative phase can proceed. The cited claim describes the proliferative phase, not the sequence.
Chronic inflammation can follow an unresolved acute episode — though it can also begin as chronic, which is why this edge is directional and not exclusive.
Spilled intracellular contents are a specific injury that triggers acute inflammation. Both endpoints are cited; the causal link is not directly asserted by either source.
Carcinogenesis produces the tumour whose properties tumour biology describes.
Grade and stage describe properties of a tumour, so the tumour must be understood first.
Cancer is uncontrolled growth, which is a failure of the controls the cell cycle describes.
Persistent stimulus in metaplastic tissue is a recognised route toward dysplasia and malignancy. The cited claim defines adaptation and does not assert the sequence.
Evading apoptosis is one of the capabilities a cell must acquire. The cited claim defines apoptosis and does not assert the link.
Students routinely conflate what a tumour is with how it is described. Recorded so the reader surfaces the distinction.
A pedigree is the instrument on which a Mendelian pattern is identified.
Mitochondrial inheritance is the pattern most reliably read off a pedigree alone.
Both patterns are independently cited; one transmits from either parent, the other from the mother alone.
A single-gene condition follows an inheritance pattern; most aneuploidies are new events and do not.
Genetic testing identifies changes in chromosomes, which is what a chromosomal disorder is.
A consultation explains, consents and interprets the testing, so the test must be understood to counsel about it.
A pedigree is drawn during the consultation and is the basis of the risk given.
The source states the distinction directly: one is the drug acting on the organism, the other the organism acting on the drug.
A dose–response curve is the quantitative form of the drug action pharmacodynamics describes.
The index is derived by comparing the effect and toxicity curves, so the curves must be understood first.
A wider index means the therapeutic and toxic doses are further apart, so adverse reactions at normal doses are less likely. Both endpoints are cited; the inverse relation is not directly asserted.
An interaction changes what a drug does, and an unintended noxious result at a normal dose is an adverse reaction.
A pharmacokinetic interaction alters absorption, distribution, metabolism or excretion, so those must be understood first.
An interaction is a cause; an adverse reaction is an outcome. Students frequently use the terms interchangeably.
Atrophy proceeds by degrading organelles including mitochondria. Weakly supported by the cited claim and recorded as such.
Absorption and distribution are membrane crossings, so lipid solubility governs both.
Mendelian genes sit on nuclear chromosomes, which is what distinguishes them from the mitochondrial genome.
A bacterium is a self-sufficient cell; a virus depends on host machinery. The cited claim states the dependence that separates them.
Fungi are eukaryotic and bacteria are not, which is the whole of the drug-target difference. The cited claim establishes the eukaryotic half.
Students routinely treat a virus as a very small bacterium. Both definitions are cited, and they do not describe the same kind of thing.
Whether presence becomes disease is what virulence measures, so the colonisation-infection boundary is read through it. The cited claim defines virulence and does not assert this ordering.
Colonisation is presence without disease; virulence is the capacity to cause it. The cited definition supplies the "without disease" half.
An organism must reach a host before it can colonise one. The cited claim describes a route of arrival and does not state the sequence.
Sterilization removes organisms from the inanimate objects that carry them, which is the vehicle route. Both endpoints are cited; neither source asserts the causal link between them.
Culture can only grow what the specimen contained, and the cited claim requires the specimen to be representative and sufficient for complete examination.
Culture is the route by which a bacterial cause is confirmed, which the cited claim states directly.

Ordered as teaching sequence rather than dependence — culture is understood first, and molecular testing is taught against it. The cited claim compares the two on sensitivity and does not establish an order.
One amplifies nucleic acid, the other grows the organism. Both cited definitions describe the different thing each detects.
The cited claim names viral infection among what PCR is the reference standard for, which is why virology relies on it where culture cannot.
Virulence factors are products of an organism, so the organism has to be understood first. The cited claim defines the factors and not the teaching order.
A parasite is defined by its relationship to a host; a bacterium by its cellular structure. The two cited definitions are of different kinds, which is the point.
The arthropod group is both a parasite category and the vector role in transmission, and conflating the two is the classic error. Both cited claims name that group.
A molecular test is as limited by the specimen as a culture is. The cited claim sets the requirement for microbiologic examination generally and does not name molecular methods.
Both are eukaryotic and both cause chronic disease, so they are grouped together in error. The cited definitions separate them by what defines each.

Both involve deliberately suppressing organisms, for opposite ends — one to remove all of them, one to reveal a chosen few. Both cited claims describe their own process and neither draws the comparison.
Decontamination is only intelligible once the vehicle route it closes is understood. The cited claim defines that route and not the teaching order.
A culture result cannot be interpreted without knowing what colonisation is, or every positive reads as infection. The cited claim defines colonisation and does not state the dependence.
Virulence factors are products of the organism, which the cited claim states, so virulence is a property carried by the organism rather than a separate entity.
The yeast-mould distinction is a growth observation, so it is made on culture. Both endpoints are cited and neither source connects them.
A thrombus must exist before a fragment of it can travel. Both cited definitions describe the two stages, and the embolism definition names a blood clot as the usual material.
The cited infarction definition names an embolus as one of the two commonest causes of the obstruction.
The cited infarction definition names a thrombus as one of the two commonest causes of the obstruction.
The cited infarction definition states that the necrosis is due to local ischaemia, which places ischaemia before it in the sequence.
The two words are used interchangeably in error. Both cited definitions are present and they describe different things: necrosis against hypoperfusion.
Embolism is taught after thrombosis because most emboli are thrombus fragments. The cited claim defines thrombosis and does not state the teaching order.
Oedema is expansion of the interstitial compartment specifically. Both cited claims are needed to see that: one names the interstitium, the other places it within the extracellular volume.
The compartments must be understood before oedema can be read as a change in one of them. Both endpoints are cited; neither source states the dependence.
The cited hypovolaemia definition is stated in terms of extracellular fluid volume, which the compartment claim defines.
The cited mechanism claim explains hyponatraemia as excess total body water relative to sodium, which presupposes the total body water the compartment claim quantifies.
Two thresholds either side of the same reference range, both cited, describing opposite deviations.
Both cited claims give the limits at opposite ends of the same narrow normal range.

Potassium and acid-base state move together across the cell membrane, and the two are read as a pair. Both endpoints are cited and neither source asserts a causal link, which is why this edge stays unverified: the direction is genuinely bidirectional in practice.
The cited source states both in one sentence, distinguishing the primary organ and the direction of compensation for each.
The compensating value in one is mistaken for a primary disorder of the other. Both cited definitions name which value moves first.
The gap is calculated to sort metabolic acidosis by cause. Both endpoints are cited; the anion gap source defines the calculation without naming that use.
The gap is only meaningful once the acidosis it subdivides is understood. Both endpoints are cited and neither states the order.

A sodium concentration is a statement about the water it is dissolved in, so the disorder belongs inside the account of body water. Both endpoints are cited and neither frames it as containment.

Ordered only so that a student calculates the gap after excluding a respiratory primary. This is a teaching convention rather than a fact, both endpoints are cited, and neither source supports the ordering.

Severe hyperkalaemia causes arrhythmia, and arrhythmia can reduce perfusion enough to infarct tissue. The chain is real but has two steps not covered by the cited claim, which names the arrhythmia only. Kept at low confidence and marked unverified rather than dropped, because students meet it.
Distribution delivers drug to the liver, where metabolism acts. Both endpoints are cited; neither source states the sequence.
The cited elimination claim states that one of the two routes is metabolic biotransformation followed by excretion, which places metabolism before excretion.
The cited claim defines the volume of distribution as the parameter describing the tendency the distribution claim names.
The cited claims place cytochrome P450 as the catalyst of phase I, and phase I as one half of metabolism.
The cited first-pass claim defines it as metabolism at a specific location, which makes it an instance of the metabolism the other claim defines.
The cited clearance claim is defined in terms of the elimination rate the other claim describes.
Half-life measures the fall in concentration produced by the elimination the other claim defines. Both are cited.
Both cited definitions describe elimination, and students use them interchangeably; one is a rate relative to concentration, the other a time.
The cited claims show that the change in older adults is in renal elimination, so excretion has to be understood before the population differences are.
Reduced renal elimination lowers clearance. Both endpoints are cited; the ageing claim names elimination rather than the clearance parameter.
The parameter cannot be read without the process it measures, and both cited definitions are in the same terms.
Two drugs competing for the same P450 enzyme is the commonest metabolic interaction. Both endpoints are cited and neither source connects them.
Less drug reaching the systemic circulation means less available to distribute. The cited claim states the fall in concentration and does not name distribution.
The cited ageing claim names metabolism as one of the two processes that decline, so metabolism must be understood first.
Impaired excretion lengthens half-life, which is how the change is seen in practice. Both endpoints are cited and neither states the link.
